item: Rear frame side boxes (pair)
model: Two green rectangular boxes sit at the very rear end of the frame, over or behind axle 4. In model-rearoblique.png the near box is at about (1035-1105,555-600) and the far box at about (1175-1245,525-570). In model-side.png the box is at about x 1120-1190, behind the axle-4 centre (x≈1135).
real: On a 543A the two tall dark boxes sit between axles 3 and 4, one on each side, on top of or just outboard of the rails. Their bottoms are roughly level with the tyre tops, and nothing box-shaped is at the rear end.
evidence: maz543a-5.jpg: left box at about (330-390,260-310), between the left wheels of axle 3 (≈300,310) and axle 4 (≈405,360); right box at about (478-540,215-265), between the right wheels of axle 3 (≈460,225) and axle 4 (≈570,280). factory-543a-profile.jpg: box at about (705-775,268-300), between axle 3 (x≈690) and axle 4 (x≈795). maz543a-4.jpg: box at about (100-140,222-250), between axle 4 (x≈65) and axle 3 (x≈160).
blenderApproach: Keep a single box object and move its origin, driven by an Empty, to the middle of the axle 3-4 gap. Build it as a Cube with a Bevel modifier (2 segments, limit by angle) and a separately Solidified lid plane. Cut the hinge and latch recesses with a Boolean, then add Bevel and Weighted Normal. Use Array (count 2) for the hinges and latches. Use a Mirror modifier across the vehicle centreline (Y) so both sides stay symmetric. Make the mounting brackets from a Curve with a rectangular bevel object that hooks onto the rail flange.

item: Frame and running-gear paint colour
model: The frame rails and cross members read as light grey or greenish grey (model-side.png, band at y≈525-550; model-top.png, light rails from x 760 to 1110).
real: On the bare 543A chassis the frame rails, cross members, suspension and driveline are painted black or very dark. Only the cab shell, the rear boxes and the wheels are in the lighter olive.
evidence: maz543a-5.jpg: the whole frame and underside, from about (200,160) to (600,350), is near-black. factory-543a-profile.jpg: the rear frame at about (555-840,270-345) is dark. maz543a-4.jpg: the rear frame at about (40-340,220-300) is dark.
blenderApproach: Assign a separate dark semi-gloss material, 'chassis_black' (base colour ≈0.03-0.05, roughness 0.6), to the rails, cross members, suspension and driveline collections. Add a Geometry Nodes or material-attribute edge-wear mask (Pointiness or bevel-based AO) for subtle lighter edges. Keep the olive only on the boxes and body.

item: Dense running gear visible between the wheels (suspension levers, torsion bars, half-shafts)
model: From the side, the gaps between axles 2-3 and 3-4 below the rails are mostly open, and the ground shows through (model-side.png at about x 1000-1080, y 555-610, and between the tank and axle 3). Suspension arms are hard to see.
real: From the side there is a solid dark mass of suspension levers, shock absorbers, torsion-bar housings and half-shafts at hub height between each pair of wheels. The gap under the frame is visually busy, not empty.
evidence: factory-543a-profile.jpg: at about (560-660,290-370) and (735-775,295-370). maz543a-4.jpg: at about (200-300,235-300) and (100-150,240-300). maz543a-5.jpg: the under-frame area around each rear wheel at about (240-300,250-320) and (430-480,280-340).
blenderApproach: Model one wheel station: a double lever arm (Boolean + Bevel + Weighted Normal plate arms with a Solidify rib), a shock absorber (a Spin-profile cylinder), a torsion-bar housing (Curve with a circular bevel) and a half-shaft (Curve bevel plus Spin-profile CV-joint boots). Instance this station on each wheel position with a Geometry Nodes 'Instance on Points' setup using axle-centre points, and Mirror it across Y. Drive it with the existing wheel-travel rig so it stays functional.

item: Air receivers / cylinders inside the frame
model: No light-grey longitudinal cylinders are visible inside the rear frame in model-rearoblique.png or model-top.png, only thin tan pipe lines along the rails.
real: Two light-grey cylinders lie along the frame inside the rails, a little behind the central housing between axles 2 and 3. Their presence is clear. Their function (most likely compressed-air receivers for the brakes and tyre-inflation system) is not confirmed.
evidence: maz543a-5.jpg: light-grey tubes at about (330-405,220-250), near the right rail, behind the central housing at about (260-320,160-215).
blenderApproach: Draw a half-profile with a domed end and use a Screw/Spin modifier (360°, 24-32 steps). Duplicate the pair with an Array modifier (relative offset in the lateral direction). Make the clamp straps from a Curve with a flat rectangular bevel wrapped around the tank, with Array + Curve modifier for the number of straps. Add air lines as Curves with a small round bevel that follow the rails to the axle stations.

item: Central transfer case with drum and driveshaft branching behind the rear cab
model: Behind the cab module the model shows only a small dark block and a single central shaft (model-rearoblique.png at about (905-960,520-545); model-top.png, a small block at x≈810 and a green block at x≈915 on the centreline).
real: Directly behind the rear cab module on the centreline there is a large dark housing with a prominent round drum or cover. Several driveshafts leave it forward and aft, and the smaller central axle-drive housings follow down the centreline.
evidence: maz543a-5.jpg: housing at about (260-320,160-215), with a round cover at about (300,205) and shafts running toward (400,250) and (470,290).
blenderApproach: Build the housing as boxes joined with Booleans, then Bevel and Weighted Normal. Make the drum or cover with a Spin modifier from a profile curve. Make each driveshaft a Curve (Bezier through the U-joint points) with a circular bevel. Place the U-joint yokes at the curve endpoints with Geometry Nodes 'Instance on Points', aligned to the curve tangent, so the shaft angles update with suspension travel.

item: Rear end of frame: rear cross beam, number-plate bracket and lamps instead of mud flaps
model: The rear ends in dark flat mud-flap-like panels hanging behind the axle-4 wheels (model-rearoblique.png at about (1240-1282,575-665) and near the left box; model-side.png, a dark plate at about x 1180-1200, y 530-565) and a round ring on the right rear (about (1190,615)).
real: The rails end in a transverse rear beam. A low number plate hangs from a bracket at the left rear, and small lamp mounts are at the corners. No full-height mud flaps are visible behind the rear wheels in any 543A bare-chassis photo, but the resolution is low.
evidence: maz543a-5.jpg: rear beam at about (480-600,290-345); number plate reading '82-17' at about (462-490,335-347) on the left rear; a vertical post or lamp at about (575-600,290-330). factory-543a-profile.jpg and maz543a-4.jpg: nothing hangs behind the axle-4 tyre at about (835-850,300-370) and (30-45,250-300).
blenderApproach: Replace the flap panels with a rear cross beam: a channel-section Curve with a U-profile bevel object, or Boolean + Bevel on a box. Add a pintle or tow-eye block (Spin-profile eye, Boolean-cut into a plate). Put a number-plate bracket (Solidify plate plus a Curve-bevel strap) on the left. Make round lamp housings with the Spin modifier on short posts, and Mirror the lamps across Y.

item: Pad or bracket blocks on the rails between axles 2 and 3 (platform mounting points)
model: The rail tops between axles 2 and 3 carry nothing (model-side.png, x≈760-950 at y≈520). The only nearby item is the green tank below the rail.
real: A lower dark block or bracket sits on top of each rail between axles 2 and 3, forward of the taller axle 3-4 boxes. These are likely support pads or brackets for the missile platform. They are clearly present, but their identity is uncertain.
evidence: factory-543a-profile.jpg: block at about (580-635,268-290). maz543a-4.jpg: block at about (200-250,222-240). maz543a-5.jpg: comparable dark structure on the right rail at about (380-420,190-210).
blenderApproach: Make one bracket (a Boolean-gusseted plate with Bevel and Weighted Normal). Scatter it along the rail with Geometry Nodes, using a Curve that follows the rail top and points at the reference stations (Resample Curve set to explicit points, then Instance on Points). Mirror it across Y so both rails get matching pads.

item: Green cylindrical tank on the left side between axles 2 and 3
model: A prominent olive horizontal cylinder hangs below the left rail between axles 2 and 3 (model-rearoblique.png at about (690-775,525-575); model-side.png at about (790-860,530-560)).
real: No olive cylindrical tank is visible in this spot on the 543A photos. The area behind the cab below the rail looks dark and cluttered instead: running gear, and possibly a dark-painted item.
evidence: factory-543a-profile.jpg: region at about (455-640,255-340) is dark with no green cylinder. maz543a-5.jpg: left side between the axle 2 (≈195,230) and axle 3 (≈300,310) wheels, at about (225-270,225-270), shows no green tank.
blenderApproach: Check this against a documented fuel-tank location before changing it. If it stays, repaint it dark and tuck it higher, inboard of the rail. If it is removed, fill the space with the running-gear station from finding 3. Any tank should be a Spin/Screw profile with strap Curves, not a scaled primitive.

item: Wheel face: projecting central hub with tyre-inflation fitting, dark disc, rim and lock-ring edge
model: The wheels show a fairly flat olive disc with a ring of round holes and a small hub (model-rearoblique.png, near wheel at about (960-1040,620-700)). No distinct projecting hub boss or central inflation swivel is readable.
real: Each wheel has a recessed dark disc and a distinct rim or lock-ring edge. At the centre is a pronounced projecting hub boss with a cap and a central air fitting for the central tyre-inflation system. The museum's white rim paint is a repaint and is not evidence of the factory colour.
evidence: museum-front-oblique.jpg: hub at about (760-900,1080-1200), with a stepped hub cap and a central fitting; the rim ring is at radius ≈0.53 of the tyre radius. factory-543a-profile.jpg: wheels at about (360-400,315-355) and (500-545,315-355) show a dark disc, a bright rim ring and a raised centre. maz543a-4.jpg: hub at about (440-460,265-285).
blenderApproach: Draw one half-section profile (lock ring, rim flange, dished disc, hub boss, cap) and revolve it with the Spin modifier (48-64 steps). Use a Bevel modifier and Weighted Normal for crisp edges. Make wheel nuts as one Spin-profile nut instanced radially with Geometry Nodes (Mesh Circle points, then Instance on Points, aligned to the normal). Add the inflation swivel as a Spin-profile valve body on the hub axis, with a short Curve-bevel air line. Size the tyre to the VI-203 sheet: outside diameter 1500 mm, section width 610 mm, 635 mm bead seat.

item: Tyre tread wrap onto the shoulders (VI-203 cross-country pattern)
model: The tyres have chunky lugs and approximately correct proportions: in model-top.png the width-to-diameter ratio is about 0.41, which matches 610/1500.
real: The VI-203 has staggered, angled block pairs that cross the centreline and run well down onto a rounded shoulder, with a smooth lettered sidewall. The 543A rear photo shows the same wrap onto the shoulders. In the model, check that blocks continue over the shoulder and that the sidewall bulges rather than being cut flat.
evidence: VI-203-manufacturer-sheet.png: tyre render at about (1160-1530,380-940). maz543a-5.jpg: tyres at about (360-460,300-420) and (275-350,255-350) show blocks wrapping over the shoulders.
blenderApproach: Build one tread pitch (a block pair) as a small mesh. Repeat it around the circumference with an Array modifier plus a Simple Deform (bend 360°), or with a Curve modifier on a circle, on top of a Spin-revolved carcass with a rounded shoulder profile. Use a Shrinkwrap or Geometry Nodes 'Sample Nearest Surface' step to conform the block bottoms to the carcass, then Bevel for the lug edges.

item: Engine/radiator top cover between the cabs
model: In exterior mode the engine is open to view between the cabs. model-front.png shows silver engine parts above the grille at about x=730-850, y=440-475. model-top.png shows the whole engine uncovered between the two cab pods (about x=455-595, y=470-555).
real: The area between the cabs is closed. museum-front.jpg shows a curved, lipped top cover over the radiator with latches and filler caps (about x=585-875, y=555-595), and nothing mechanical shows above it. In maz543a-4.jpg (about x=650-720, y=110-205) and maz543a-7.jpg (about x=85-210, y=55-200) the space between the cabs is a closed dark hood and grille box. REFERENCE_NOTES line 56 agrees: the grille has its own frame and a shallow hinged top surface. The tall panel at roof height behind it in museum-front.jpg (x=600-820, y=440-550) may belong to the museum vehicle's installed equipment, so leave that part out.
evidence: model-front.png, model-top.png vs museum-front.jpg (hood lip y=555-595), maz543a-4.jpg, maz543a-7.jpg
blenderApproach: Draw the hood cross-section as one Bezier curve (flat top, rolled front lip). Extrude it across the gap with a Curve object, or give a plane a Solidify modifier and shape the lip with a Bevel profile. Cut the hinge seams and a filler-cap recess with Boolean (difference) cutters, then add Bevel (limit method: angle, 2-3 segments) and Weighted Normal. Place the latches with an Array modifier along the lip, and Mirror everything about the vehicle centreline.

item: Front bumper depth and shape
model: The bumper is a thin bar only about 15% of the nose height. In model-front.png it runs about y=560-585 with orange lamps at the ends. In model-frontoblique.png it is about x=360-560, y=570-610. Two separate round towing eyes hang below it (model-front about (678,597) and (886,597)).
real: The bumper is a massive dark box beam, roughly one third of the cab front height below the lamps. museum-front.jpg: about x=410-1040, y=705-790. It is split into two halves by a central recessed notch that holds a single tow hook (about x=720-745, y=750-800), and a dark lower skid plate sits behind it (y=790-835). From the side (museum-front-oblique.jpg, about x=175-320, y=930-1045) each end is a large trapezoidal plate whose lower edge slopes back up under the cab. maz543a-7.jpg (x=10-300, y=195-245) and maz543a-4.jpg (x=600-755, y=205-240) show the same deep beam standing ahead of the cabs.
evidence: model-front.png, model-frontoblique.png vs museum-front.jpg, museum-front-oblique.jpg, maz543a-7.jpg, maz543a-4.jpg
blenderApproach: Draw one closed curve for the beam section (a tall rectangle chamfered at the bottom) and sweep it along a straight path curve with Bevel Object. Alternatively, use a box with a Mirror (X) modifier, Boolean-cut the centre notch and the sloped end cut-backs, then add Bevel (angle limit) and Weighted Normal. Make the end plates as planar trapezoids with Solidify. Place the bolt heads with Array along a curve. Replace the two eyes with one hook built from a Screw/Spin profile set in the notch.

item: Windscreen height and outline
model: The windscreen is short and the metal below it is tall. In model-front.png the image-left cab has its roof at about y=400, glass at about y=408-462 and bumper top at about y=560, so the glass is about 34% of the height from roof to bumper. At this resolution the opening reads as a plain rounded rectangle.
real: The glass is about 47-49% of the height from roof to bumper. museum-front.jpg: roof about y=460, glass about y=475-590, bumper top about y=705. maz543a-7.jpg left cab: roof about y=55, glass about y=62-130, bumper about y=195. The glass is a rounded polygon with a thick rubber frame and a pronounced diagonal lower inner corner (museum-front.jpg about x=575-595, y=560-590 and x=855-875, y=560-600; REFERENCE_NOTES line 53). The CAB_PHOTO_FIT_NOTES already lists this windshield and nose-height difference as unresolved.
evidence: model-front.png vs museum-front.jpg, maz543a-7.jpg; CAB_PHOTO_FIT_NOTES.md lines 19-20
blenderApproach: Draw the opening as a 2D curve (rounded polygon with the diagonal inner corner) and make it about 35-40% taller downward. Cut it from the cab front shell with Boolean difference, then add Bevel (3 segments, angle limit) and Weighted Normal. Build the rubber gasket from the same curve with a small rounded-rectangle Bevel Object profile, and the glass as a Fill of the curve with a thin Solidify. Mirror across the vehicle centreline, inverting the diagonal for the other cab.

item: Roof searchlight position
model: The searchlight sits near the rear edge of a cab roof. In model-top.png it is at about (557,450), at the rear of the image-top cab, which is the vehicle's right cab when the front faces image-left. model-side.png shows it at about x=570 at the cab's rear end, and model-front.png shows it on the image-left cab, which again is the vehicle's right.
real: The searchlight is on the left (driver's) cab, at the front roof edge just above the windscreen and slightly inboard. museum-front.jpg: about x=885, y=400-440 on the image-right cab, which is the vehicle's left. museum-front-oblique.jpg, which shows the left side: about x=350-380, y=600-640 near the front of the roof. maz543a-7.jpg: about x=250, y=10-45 directly above the left cab's windscreen. maz543a-4.jpg: about (685,95) on the far (left) cab's front.
evidence: model-top.png, model-side.png, model-front.png vs museum-front.jpg, museum-front-oblique.jpg, maz543a-7.jpg, maz543a-4.jpg
blenderApproach: Move the lamp assembly to the left cab's front roof edge. Model the lamp housing by spinning a half-profile curve with Spin/Screw (360°, about 24 steps), then add Solidify and a lens disc from the same revolve. Make the short pedestal and yoke from a curve with round Bevel. Add the wire guard as a circle curve with Bevel, repeated with an Array modifier (rotation offset through an Empty).

item: Rear-view mirrors on long arms
model: Only small stubs sit close to the cab sides. In model-front.png they are at about x=598-606 and x=958-966, at y=430-445 and y=520-530. They project only about 3-4% of the overall width beyond the cabs.
real: Each mirror is carried on a long bent tubular arm from the lower outer front corner of the cab, with the head at about headlamp height and well outside the cab width (about 9% of overall width). museum-front.jpg: arm from about (430,700) to a head at about (368,650), and from about (1030,700) to (1075,660). museum-front-oblique.jpg shows the same arm edge-on as a post with a round head at about x=180-200, y=855-935. A thin rod also rises from the upper front corner (museum-front-oblique.jpg x=240-275, y=705-800; museum-front.jpg x=1015-1030, y=520-600).
evidence: model-front.png vs museum-front.jpg, museum-front-oblique.jpg
blenderApproach: Make each arm a Bezier curve with round Bevel depth, plus a slight Taper curve for the thicker root. Make the mirror head by spinning a dish profile with Spin, then add Solidify. Reuse the same Bevel curve technique for the thin rod at the upper corner. Mirror modifier with the vehicle centreline Empty as mirror object.

item: Hanging tubular boarding step under the doors
model: No hanging tube step is distinguishable below the doors. In model-side.png, below the doors (about x=455-575, y=520-545) only the chassis and the first wheel are visible. Could be too small to resolve in the screenshot.
real: A long U-shaped tubular step hangs well below the cab floor under both doors, ahead of the first wheel, on about three vertical hanger tubes. museum-front-oblique.jpg: about x=395-625, y=1020-1095. REFERENCE_NOTES line 57 also records a step hanging below the doors in front of the wheel.
evidence: model-side.png vs museum-front-oblique.jpg; REFERENCE_NOTES.md line 57
blenderApproach: Draw a single poly/Bezier curve for the U-frame and give it round Bevel depth. Instance the hanger tubes with Geometry Nodes (Instance on Points on the curve's resampled points), or use a short tube with an Array modifier. Mirror for the right cab.

item: Lower nose chamfer of each cab
model: In model-frontoblique.png and model-side.png the cab front looks near-vertical from the windscreen down to the thin bumper (model-side about x=390-400, y=425-535). No strong swept-back lower face is readable.
real: museum-front-oblique.jpg shows the lower front face just below the headlamp standing slightly ahead of the windscreen line. Below the headlamp it chamfers back steeply to the cab floor, from about (245,900) to (330,1015), and the bumper end plate attaches to that slope. The near cab in maz543a-7.jpg shows a similar sloped lower front (about x=210-300, y=185-215).
evidence: model-side.png, model-frontoblique.png vs museum-front-oblique.jpg, maz543a-7.jpg
blenderApproach: Define the cab side silhouette as one closed 2D curve: raked windscreen line, small forward bulge at headlamp level, about 40-45° chamfer to the floor. Extrude it to cab width, or drive the cab with a Geometry Nodes 'Curve to Mesh + Extrude' setup. Finish with Bevel (angle limit) and Weighted Normal so the chamfer edge stays crisp.

item: Rear box behind the cabs: rounded rear edge and roof louvers
model: The box behind the cabs is flat-topped with sharp edges. It has a vertical rear face with a red element (model-rearoblique.png about x=560-690, y=365-450) and a louver panel on the side (model-side.png about x=655-765, y=450-475).
real: maz543a-4.jpg shows a large-radius rounded rear top corner on this enclosure (about x=340-370, y=110-190). maz543a-5.jpg shows a raised roof section with louvers (about x=150-250, y=40-90) and a rear face with vertical stiffening ribs that slants rather than standing vertical (about x=230-330, y=60-150). factory-543a-profile.jpg also shows a sloped rear top (about x=440-490, y=150-200).
evidence: model-rearoblique.png, model-side.png vs maz543a-4.jpg, maz543a-5.jpg, factory-543a-profile.jpg
blenderApproach: Build the enclosure from one side-profile curve (with the rear radius and slant) extruded to width, then add Solidify and Bevel. Make the ribs with Array along the rear face and the roof louvers with Array of a Boolean-cut slat. Apply Bevel and Weighted Normal after the Booleans.

item: Small windows in the cab inner walls
model: The inner walls facing the engine gap cannot be judged in the model screenshots (model-front.png shows them edge-on; in model-frontoblique.png about x=440-520, y=400-470 no clear window can be seen).
real: Each cab has a small window in its inner wall facing the gap. museum-front.jpg: a light glazed rectangle in the left cab's inner wall at about x=825-842, y=495-555. maz543a-7.jpg: a rounded window in the right cab's inner wall above the grille at about x=110-165, y=72-105.
evidence: museum-front.jpg, maz543a-7.jpg vs model-frontoblique.png
blenderApproach: Reuse the same rounded-window cutter curve as the side glass. Boolean it into the inner wall and finish with Bevel and Weighted Normal. Make the gasket as a curve with a Bevel Object profile. Mirror for the other cab.

item: Tubular ladder guard on the radiator grille
model: The grille face is plain vertical slats in a frame (model-front.png about x=705-857, y=475-560).
real: museum-front.jpg shows a ladder-like tubular guard bolted across the grille face: two horizontal rails with about 5 vertical rungs (about x=635-845, y=600-690). The small factory photos (maz543a-7.jpg, factory-543a-profile.jpg) cannot confirm it, so it may be a later or field fitting.
evidence: museum-front.jpg vs model-front.png
blenderApproach: Make the two rails as Bezier curves with round Bevel. Place the rungs as one tube with an Array modifier (count 5, fit length), or with Geometry Nodes Instance on Points along a rail. Add standoff brackets with Array.

item: Engine/cooling housing behind cabs: length and rear-edge position
model: The housing side runs from about axle 1 (x≈580) to x≈767, so it is about 187 px ≈ 2.55 m long. Its rear edge is about 0.5 m BEHIND the axle-2 centre (axle 2 at x≈730).
real: The housing ends AHEAD of axle 2. In factory-543a-profile the housing runs from the cab rear x≈372 to x≈490 against a near axle-2 centre at x≈510, with axle 1 to axle 2 = 140 px (2.2 m). That gives about 1.85 m length, with the rear edge about 0.3 m ahead of axle 2. maz543a-4 shows the housing at x≈341–455 against axle-2 centre ≈318 and axle-1 ≈458, giving about 1.8 m and a rear edge about 0.35 m ahead of axle 2. The model housing is therefore about 35–40% too long, with its rear end about 0.8 m too far back.
evidence: factory-543a-profile.jpg: housing rear edge found by sky contrast at x≈488–493 for rows y=180–240, near wheels centred at x≈370/510. maz543a-4.jpg: housing rear edge x≈341–344 at rows y=150–190, wheels at x≈458/318. model-side.png: housing olive columns x=600–760, y 429–503, tyre chords at row 605 centred at 571/730.
blenderApproach: Rebuild the housing shell as one cross-section profile curve (Bezier) swept along a straight X path with Geometry Nodes Curve to Mesh (Fill Caps on). Drive the path end with a driver = axle2_x − ~0.3 m and the start with the cab rear, so the length follows the axle layout. Add Solidify (panel thickness), then Bevel (limit by angle, 2 segments), then Weighted Normal. Door/access cutouts stay as Boolean cutters parented to the same path so they move with the length.

item: Rear frame boxes: placement relative to axles 3/4
model: The boxes sit on the rails over and behind axle 4. In the side view they are at x≈1060–1190 against an axle-4 centre at x≈1131. In model-rearoblique they are at x≈1035–1110 against a near axle-4 wheel at ≈1000, with the far box at ≈1170–1260. The boxes are low and flat.
real: There is one box on each rail BETWEEN axles 3 and 4, ahead of axle 4. maz543a-5 shows the near box at x≈330–390, y≈262–310 between near axle 3 (≈310) and axle 4 (≈405), and the far box at x≈478–540 between far axles ≈465/575. The boxes look roughly cubic with a lid. factory-543a-profile shows the near box at x≈700–780 between axle 3 (≈700) and axle 4 (≈795). maz543a-4 shows a box at x≈85–145 between axle 4 (≈70) and axle 3 (≈160). A second box between axles 2 and 3 (factory x≈575–630; maz543a-4 x≈205–250) may be on the near or the far rail.
evidence: maz543a-5.jpg: boxes on both rails in the 3–4 bay. factory-543a-profile.jpg: box on the near rail x≈700–780, y≈268–300. maz543a-4.jpg: x≈85–145, y≈222–245. Model: model-side.png x≈1060–1190, y≈498–535, and model-rearoblique.png.
blenderApproach: Place the boxes with Geometry Nodes Instance on Points. Compute the point X as axle3_x + ~0.55·(axle4_x − axle3_x) at rail-top Z, mirrored in Y. Build the box from a cube with Bevel (limit by angle), then Solidify, then Weighted Normal. Add the lid seam and hinge line as a thin Boolean groove, then Bevel. Keep the optional 2–3-bay box as a separate instance, off by default until its side is confirmed.

item: Housing side: large horizontal slatted louvre and hatch not seen on 543A
model: The left housing side carries a long horizontal slatted louvre (x≈660–760, y≈445–475, about 1.4 m × 0.4 m) and a hinged hatch with handle ahead of it (x≈600–650). The side panel is otherwise one flat plane down to y≈503.
real: In factory-543a-profile the left housing side (x≈378–490, y≈160–245) is a plain panel. Where the model louvre would sit (x≈430–485, y≈165–190) the luminance is a uniform ~145–155 with no dark slot band. At 880 px a 1.4 m louvre would show as roughly 60×15 px. The one clear feature is a horizontal break at about 55% of the housing height (y≈207): the panel above is lighter and the band below is darker, from y 210 to 245. maz543a-4 shows the same on the right side: a plain upper panel (y≈140–162), a break at y≈163 and a darker lower band to y≈198. There is also a vertical dark seam between the cab rear and the lower housing front (factory x≈378–384, y≈204–228). maz543a-4 may show a narrow, vertical-format panel of horizontal slats at the extreme rear of the side (x≈344–372), but this is not certain.
evidence: factory-543a-profile.jpg pixel rows y=162–246 across x=378–490. maz543a-4.jpg columns x=350–430. model-side.png louvre at x≈660–760.
blenderApproach: Remove the side louvre and hatch instances. Cut the horizontal break line with a thin box Boolean (Difference), then Bevel (2 segments), then Weighted Normal. Make the lower band a 20–40 mm inset step in the housing profile curve rather than separate geometry. If the narrow rear-end louvre is confirmed, build the slats as a curve with bevel/taper profile and repeat them with an Array modifier (relative offset in Z) inside a Boolean-cut frame.

item: Overall roof height vs tyre diameter (cab/housing body too short)
model: The roof is at y≈429 and the ground at ≈624, with tyre D ≈109 px. Roof/D ≈ 1.79, about 2.68 m. The cab sill is at ≈0.82 D and the frame top at ≈0.94 D, both correct. The cab body from roof to sill is ≈0.97 D.
real: factory-543a-profile gives roof ≈138 against wheel 1 at x≈370 spanning ≈265–398, so roof/D ≈ 1.98. maz543a-4 gives roof ≈107–112 against a tyre at ≈218–332 (x≈455–460), so roof/D ≈ 1.93–1.97. The MAZ-543 drawing values in REFERENCE_NOTES (height 2900 mm with a 1500 mm tyre) give 1.93. The museum side photo (543-family, wide-angle) gives ≈1.82. The sill and frame heights agree with the model, so the shortfall of about 7–10% is in the body height between sill and roof.
evidence: factory-543a-profile.jpg column x≈350–372. maz543a-4.jpg columns x≈455–470. museum-front-oblique.jpg roof y≈645, tyre y≈940–1300. model-side.png columns x=420–760 and x=571.
blenderApproach: Add one shared Lattice modifier, or a Geometry Nodes Transform Geometry with its pivot at sill height, to the cab shells, housing, window and door Boolean cutters and roof fittings. Raise the roof by roughly 7% of overall height without moving the sill, wheels or frame. Check it with a camera matched in fSpy to factory-543a-profile.jpg before committing.

item: Centre engine cover between/behind the cabs: raised top missing, engine left open
model: The side silhouette is a flat line at y≈429 from the cab front to the housing end; only the beacon rises above it. From the front (model-front x≈715–850, y≈420–480) and from the top (model-top x≈455–590), the gap between the cabs is open and the engine is visible. The housing roof carries 6 flush square hatches (model-top x≈610–720).
real: A dark raised block rises above the roof line in two 543A bare-chassis photos. In factory-543a-profile it is at x≈255–335, y≈133–139, about 6 px above a roof edge at ≈142. In maz543a-4 it is at x≈490–530, y≈96–103, above the sky-lit roof. In museum-front (543A) the centre section between the cabs is closed by a front wall (x≈605–820, y≈440–560) whose top (≈440) sits at or above the cab roofs (≈455), with two dark arched notches at its lower corners (x≈610–650 and 760–810). maz543a-5 shows a raised box/hump on the housing roof (x≈150–250, y≈15–50) with small grilles on its slope. The exact outline is hard to resolve at this resolution.
evidence: factory-543a-profile.jpg columns x=270–330, rows y 133–139. maz543a-4.jpg column x=500, rows 96–103. museum-front.jpg centre section. maz543a-5.jpg housing top. Model: model-front.png, model-top.png, model-side.png.
blenderApproach: Add a closed centre cover from behind the grille to the housing: a cube with Bevel (limit by angle), then Solidify, then Weighted Normal, with its top at or slightly above the cab roof. Cut the two arched lower notches with a Boolean using a half-cylinder cutter made by Spin (180°), then Bevel. Put the roof hump on the housing as a second bevelled box, with its sloped faces made by Simple Deform (Taper). Replace the 6 flush hatches with small grilles on the hump: an Array of curve-bevel slats inside a Boolean-cut frame.

item: Housing cross-section: chamfered upper side band
model: The housing side is a flat vertical wall that meets the flat roof at a near-square edge (model-frontoblique x≈770–910, roof edge y≈400; model-side y≈429).
real: maz543a-4 shows a bright, sky-lit band just under the housing roof edge (y≈120–135 at x=400–430) above a crease at y≈137. That indicates an inward-sloping upper band over roughly the top quarter of the side. factory-543a-profile shows a lighter strip just below the roof lip (y≈162–168). In maz543a-5 the housing roof reads as a narrower plateau with sloping upper sides.
evidence: maz543a-4.jpg columns x=380–430, y 117–140. factory-543a-profile.jpg rows y 156–168. maz543a-5.jpg housing x≈125–335.
blenderApproach: Put the chamfer into the same profile curve used for the housing sweep in item 1, with the upper band sloping inward over roughly the top quarter of the side height. Alternatively, add a bevel weight on the two top longitudinal edges and use a Bevel modifier (limit by weight, 1 segment, large width) ahead of Solidify, then Weighted Normal.

item: Large rear mudflaps behind axle 4
model: Wide flat black mudflaps hang behind both axle-4 wheels (model-rearoblique x≈1240–1285, y≈575–670).
real: In maz543a-5 the tail is fully visible: the rear beam, the plate '82-17' at x≈460–490, y≈330–345, and the grass behind the near axle-4 wheel (x≈405). No mudflap is visible. None shows behind the last wheel in factory-543a-profile (x≈795–840) or maz543a-4 (x≈35–110) either.
evidence: maz543a-5.jpg rear beam area x≈440–580, y≈290–345. model-rearoblique.png mudflaps.
blenderApproach: Move the mudflaps into a separate optional collection, hidden for the bare-chassis 543A baseline. If a later-variant option is wanted, keep them as a Solidify-on-plane with a Simple Deform bend. Do not bake them into the chassis mesh.

item: Olive cylindrical fuel tank on the left rail between axles 2 and 3
model: A large olive horizontal cylinder is mounted low, outboard of the left frame rail between axles 2 and 3 (model-side x≈790–860, y≈535–565; model-rearoblique x≈690–775, y≈525–580).
real: The near side between axle 2 (≈510) and axle 3 (≈700) in factory-543a-profile shows the frame, a crossmember and a dark box on the rail top (x≈575–630, y≈268–288), but no outboard olive cylinder. maz543a-5 shows the near rail between axles 2 and 3 (x≈200–300) with pipe runs. Its dark cylinders at about x≈320–400, y≈215–250 appear to lie between the rails, not outboard. Tank location is not established from these photos.
evidence: factory-543a-profile.jpg x≈555–640, y≈265–330. maz543a-5.jpg frame bay 2–3. model-side.png and model-rearoblique.png.
blenderApproach: Hold the tank in a toggleable collection until a 543A source confirms it. If it moves between the rails, rebuild it as a Spin/Screw-revolved profile (dished ends), then Bevel and Weighted Normal. Hang it on strap brackets made as curve-bevel bands, and place it with Geometry Nodes relative to the rail and crossmember positions.
